lines.line: Summary: A tough monster that throws green fireballs from a distance and claws you up close. It has 500 hit points, and in Doom 64 it is less pale than the standard Hell knight and looks more like the baron of Hell.

quoted: Hell knights have both melee and distance attacks, scratching at close range and throwing green fireballs from a distance.
Possessing 500 hit points, Hell knights present a significant challenge to the player
Data not listed is the same as for the original version.
the variant found in Doom 64 is less pale in color, and more closely resembles Doom's baron of Hell.

lines.line: Weak points: It rarely flinches, so the rocket launcher, plasma gun and super shotgun are the best answers, and the chaingun and shotgun also work at close range. Do not fight it in melee: it claws back, and the chainsaw is ineffective against it.

quoted: They have a low pain chance that makes the rocket launcher, plasma gun and super shotgun the most effective weapons against them. The chaingun and shotgun are also effective at close range.
It is not recommended to use a melee attack due to their own scratching melee attack
It is ineffective against Hell knights and other demons with powerful attacks and low pain chance.

lines.line: Tips: Its fireballs are faster than an imp's or a cacodemon's and hit hard, but from a distance you can dodge them without much trouble. In Doom 64 Hell knights and barons of Hell can hurt each other with their fireballs, so infighting between the two is possible.

quoted: Hell knight fireballs are faster than imp and cacodemon fireballs and inflict heavy damage.
With sufficient distance, the projectiles can be dodged without much difficulty
they can deal and receive missile damage to and from barons of Hell, so infighting between the two monsters is possible.

lines.line: Summary: One of the toughest monsters in the game, with 1000 hit points; it claws up close and throws fireballs from a distance. In Doom 64 it is red-orange and throws red fireballs, and the green colour goes to the Hell knight instead.

quoted: With 1000 hit points, barons are the most resilient of all creatures in Doom save for the cyberdemon and the spiderdemon.
They attack opponents by scratching when close

The baron of Hell in Doom 64 is given a red-orange color scheme, rather than green, which is instead used for the Hell knight. They behave the same but launch red projectiles and have a smaller hitbox.

lines.line: Weak points: It rarely flinches, so use the rocket launcher, plasma gun or super shotgun. The chaingun and shotgun also work if you can stay at a distance, but they take a while. Melee is risky because you can be clawed.

quoted: Because barons take very heavy beatings before going down, and because their pain chance is low, use of the rocket launcher, plasma rifle, or super shotgun is recommended.
provided that the player can get at sufficient range without being hit, the chaingun and shotgun will also work, but may take a while.
Melee attacks against them are hazardous, as they put the player at risk of being clawed.

lines.line: Tips: Its fireballs are not too hard to dodge when you have room, especially by circle-strafing, but in a confined space it is much more dangerous. In Doom 64 barons and Hell knights hurt each other with their fireballs and so can end up fighting each other.

quoted: given sufficient space, their fireballs are not too hard to dodge (especially by circlestrafing).
In confined spaces, however, they are hard to move around and can be more lethal.
In Doom 64 barons can also injure and infight with Hell knights, and vice versa.

lines.line: Summary: A slow, wide monster with flamethrower arms that spits fireballs in bursts. In Doom 64 it is taller, wears a metal harness with a fuel pack on its back, and its fireballs are smaller and look like fiery brimstone. It first appears in MAP09: Even Simpler.

quoted: its arms have been replaced by huge flamethrowers
They first appear in MAP09: Even Simpler, a follow-up to the Doom II map.
until all three bursts have been discharged
is significantly taller, and wears a metal body harness with a fuel pack on the back. Its fireballs are smaller and appear more like fiery brimstone.

lines.line: Weak points: It is slow and a big target, so rapid-fire weapons kill it easily, and the rocket launcher is possibly the most effective weapon against it. It pauses and gives a battle cry before it fires, so even a slow weapon such as the super shotgun can stun it out of attacking.

quoted: It is slow and makes a large target, so is easy to kill with rapid-fire weapons. The rocket launcher is possibly the most effective weapon against the mancubus.
because it will pause briefly before attacking, giving out a distinctive battle cry before firing, it is easy to prevent the attacking using slower weapons to stun, even the super shotgun.

lines.line: Tips: Keep your distance: up close you may take two fireballs instead of one. Once it starts attacking it keeps firing until all three bursts are done, even if you step out of its sight, unless you hurt it mid-burst; you can use that to start monster infighting. In Doom 64 the direction of its fireballs is somewhat different from Doom II.

quoted: When a mancubus does attack, it is helpful to attempt to keep one's distance. Otherwise, the player might take two fireballs instead of just one.
Once a mancubus has begun to attack its target, it continues to fire (if it remains unhurt while firing) until all three bursts have been discharged, even if the target has moved out of its sight.
This characteristic of their attack can be abused to cause monster infighting.
Their function is otherwise the same, although the direction of the fireballs they shoot is somewhat different.

lines.line: Summary: A cybernetic brain on a big metal spider body. In Doom 64 it has two plasma guns that fire two blue bolts at once in spurts of five, and it keeps firing as long as it can see you. It first appears in MAP14: Eye of the Storm, unless you play the secret levels MAP30: The Lair and MAP32: Hectic first, which also hold some.

quoted: The arachnotron is a cybernetic spider-like monster introduced in Doom II.
the mechanical body is much bigger
Its biological body consists primarily of a large brain with two small arms
This body is seated into a metal chassis

the Doom 64 arachnotrons possess two guns that fire out two blue plasma bolt shots simultaneously, but done so in spurts of five instead of a constant rate of fire, though it will continue firing as long as it can see the player.
They first appear in MAP14: Eye of the Storm unless the player goes through MAP30: The Lair and MAP32: Hectic, which contain arachnotrons but chronologically come first.
MAP30: The Lair (secret level)
MAP32: Hectic (secret level)

lines.line: Weak points: It has a medium pain chance, so rapid-fire weapons such as the chaingun work well. Do not use the chainsaw on it: its size stops the attack reliably connecting.

quoted: They have a medium pain chance, so rapid fire weapons such as the chaingun will work well.
Using the chainsaw on them is inadvisable due to their size, which prevents the attack from reliably connecting.

lines.line: Tips: Its plasma bursts are among the fastest projectiles around and its high rate of fire can drain your health quickly. Keep attacking, move in broad side-to-side steps and slip out of its line of fire now and then, and you will take little damage. In monster infighting the Doom 64 version often beats even a baron of Hell, but with little health left.

quoted: their plasma bursts are among the fastest projectiles, and their high rate of fire can quickly drain the player's health.
If a player constantly attacks, moves in broad side-to-side movements, and tries to get out of the arachnotron's line of fire periodically, then the player will sustain minimal damage.
In Doom 64, with their new twin plasma cannons, when provoked into infighting, they will often win even against barons of Hell, but with little health remaining.

lines.line: Summary: A floating monster with a big mouth that spits balls of lightning and bites. In Doom 64 it is beige-brown with a single yellow-green eye and two arms with broken chains, and it swings its arms as it flies.

quoted: Cacodemons float slowly through the air
a large wickedly grinning mouth
Cacodemons attack by spitting a ball of lightning, or by biting with their gaping maw.
becoming beige brown, with a single yellow-green eye, and gaining two arms with broken chains attached
mostly in the way it swings its arms when in flight

lines.line: Weak points: It is slow and flinches easily, so repeating weapons such as the chaingun or the plasma gun push it away until it can barely fight back. The chainsaw can also stun it.

quoted: Because they are slow, and because their pain chance is high, they are fairly easy targets. The chainsaw can incapacitate them, and repeating weapons such as the chaingun or the plasma gun are very effective against them, as they are pushed away and are nearly unable to fight back.

lines.line: Tips: Its shots are fairly easy to dodge, and with enough room you can fight several at once and take little or no damage. Once alerted it can come flying out of unexpected places. On the Nintendo 64 its shots fly faster than on PC, though the cacodemon itself still moves slowly.

quoted: Cacodemon attacks are relatively easy to dodge, and with sufficient space large numbers of cacodemons can be fought while sustaining little or no injury.
it is not uncommon to see cacodemons flying out of unexpected places once alerted.

The change to the projectiles' speed is kept in ports based off this version, notably the Sony PlayStation version as well as Doom 64, although cacodemons move slower in the latter just as they do in the original DOS version.

lines.line: Summary: A floating monster that spits lost souls at you instead of firing a shot. In Doom 64 it is dark pink with a green eye and two mouths in place of arms, so it can spawn two lost souls at the same time, and it gives a low sinister laugh when it spots you.

quoted: Instead of shooting a standard projectile, the pain elemental periodically spews lost souls at its opponents
It is colored dark pink, has a green eye and in place of its arms are two mouths so it can now spawn two lost souls at the same time.
It gives off a low sinister laugh when it has sighted the player.

lines.line: Weak points: Focus on the pain elemental itself and leave its lost souls until it is dead. Fast-firing weapons such as the chaingun or the plasma gun work fairly well and usually keep the lost souls at bay. The rocket launcher is not recommended, because it may spit a lost soul while your rocket is in flight, and the blast can hurt you.

quoted: As such, it is vital to focus one's attention on the pain elemental itself as much as possible.

Fast-firing weapons such as the chainsaw, chaingun or plasma gun work fairly well and usually keep its lost souls at bay, but the rocket launcher is not recommended as the pain elemental may spit a lost soul while the rocket is en route, potentially causing blast damage to the player.
Only once it is dead is it recommended to begin killing its minions.

lines.line: Tips: Do not stand at point-blank range to stop it spawning, as you could in other versions: in Doom 64 every lost soul that fails to appear, including the ones it spawns when it dies, explodes with damage like an exploding barrel, and two together are roughly a rocket hit. It only spawns lost souls while you are in its line of sight, so hit it hard, then head for cover.

quoted: Unlike other versions of the game, standing at point-blank range to prevent it from spawning lost souls is not a viable option.
Each lost soul that fails to materialize, including the ones it spawns at death, will cause a significant amount of damage comparable to an exploding barrel
getting hit by both is roughly the same as being hit by a rocket.

Pain elementals will only spawn lost souls when in line of sight of the player, or another monster who struck it. Therefore an effective tactic against the pain elemental is to deliver a strong attack, then quickly head for cover.

lines.line: Summary: A towering demon with a rocket launcher mounted on its left arm and 4000 hit points. In Doom 64 it has darker skin and is much larger than on PC, and its rockets leave smoke trails. It is rare, appearing chiefly in the secret levels or late in the game.

quoted: a large rocket launcher mounted on its left arm
It attacks by firing barrages of three rockets. It has 4000 hit points and does not receive splash damage from explosions, making it fairly difficult to kill.
Data not listed is the same as for the original version.
they have darker colored skin, are slightly stronger and much larger.
The cyberdemon's rockets leave smoke trails
Cyberdemons are relatively rare throughout the game, appearing chiefly in the secret levels or later in the game.

lines.line: Weak points: The BFG9000 is the most effective weapon against it, and the plasma gun works fairly well. The rocket launcher also works, but it is a long fight, and rockets must hit it directly because it takes no blast damage. Other weapons and melee take far longer, so avoid them.

quoted: The BFG9000 is the most effective weapon against a cyberdemon, although the plasma gun can work fairly well.
If a BFG9000 is not available, the rocket launcher is also effective
but be prepared for a long fight
the cyberdemon and the spiderdemon take only direct hit damage, and are immune to all blast damage.
Killing a cyberdemon with other weapons is significantly more difficult
It is extremely difficult to kill a cyberdemon with melee attacks

lines.line: Tips: It rarely flinches, so you cannot easily stop it attacking: circle-strafe and avoid every rocket, because one will often badly hurt you. In Doom 64 its rockets are faster and come out of the launcher itself, so they head downward at you and can burst on the floor near you, even when no wall is close. On the Watch Me Die skill level, MAP17: Watch Your Step ends with two cyberdemons and MAP24: No Escape has three.

quoted: Because a cyberdemon has a low pain chance, it is difficult to prevent it from attacking.
Circle-strafing can be used to avoid return fire while attacking. Because one rocket will often be enough to critically injure the player, it is imperative that all rockets are avoided.
its rockets are faster, with their movement speed being buffed from 700 u/s up to 900 u/s.
its rockets now have a firing offset that has them emerge from the launcher itself instead of from the middle of the monster.

this results in the rockets being fired in a downward angle towards the player when on levelled height, making splash damage a greater threat as the rockets can hit the ground and explode near the player, meaning the 64 cyberdemon does not need the aid of walls for its splash damage to be a factor.
MAP17: Watch Your Step featuring a dual cyberdemon battle at the end on the Watch Me Die difficulty, while MAP24: No Escape contains three cyberdemons on Watch Me Die

lines.line: Summary: A flaming flying skull that charges at you with open jaws. In Doom 64 it has black horns and an open skull with fire only on top, and it recovers from each attack much faster than on PC. It attacks viciously, which makes it one of the most dangerous enemies in Doom 64.

quoted: Lost souls use themselves as weapons, charging towards the player with open jaws.

The Doom 64 variant of the lost soul sports black-colored horns, and has an opened skull with fire emerging only from its top. It is much more aggressive than its DOS counterpart, with a much faster recovery time from its attack.
lost souls are weaker with less health, but attack viciously, making them one of the most dangerous enemies

lines.line: Weak points: It is weaker than on PC: a single shotgun blast can fell it. You can stop a charge by shooting it while it is attacking, and a chaingun is useful against a crowd, because a shot lost soul becomes helpless until it hits something.

quoted: it is also physically weaker than its DOS counterpart and can be felled with a single shotgun blast.
The player can stop a lost soul's charge by shooting it while it is attacking.
Similarly, a chaingun can be useful against a crowd of lost souls
if shot when charging, a lost soul becomes essentially helpless until it hits something.

lines.line: Tips: It is completely silent when it spots you, so the hissing breath as it launches is often the first warning. Do not use rockets on a group: a lost soul may suddenly fly at you and make a rocket blow up close enough to hurt you. They are more often found in groups than alone.

quoted: Unlike all other monsters, the lost soul is completely silent when alerted
launches itself towards its target at high speed with a hissing breath sound, often the first audible warning of their presence.

Using rockets against groups of lost souls is strongly discouraged, as there is a considerable chance that a lost soul will suddenly fly towards the player, causing one of the rockets to explode close enough to cause blast damage to the foolish marine.
they are more often found in groups.

lines.line: Summary: Fast monsters that only attack up close. Doom 64's manual calls the demon the bull demon; it has black horns, small red eyes, bigger teeth and claws, and a slightly longer melee reach than on PC. The spectre is the same kind of monster, but in Doom 64 it starts as an opaque green-tinted demon and turns see-through once it spots you.

quoted: are unique in their exclusivity to melee attacks
the demon's fast speed and zig-zag motions

the manual refers to the monster as the "bull demon". It is given a more menacing appearance, with black horns, smaller red eyes, and accentuated teeth and claws. It also has a slightly higher melee range.
In Doom 64 specifically, inactive spectres are initially rendered as opaque demons with a green tint (a nod back to the nightmare spectre), becoming translucent upon detecting the player.

lines.line: Weak points: They have no ranged attack, so they are no threat at long range. The super shotgun can kill a demon at close range with one blast, a shotgun used hit-and-run works too, and the chaingun is also effective. The chainsaw stops a demon attacking while you saw it, and uses no ammo.

quoted: Demons do not have a ranged attack, so they are no threat at long range.
The shotgun is quite effective if you use hit and run, blasting them at close range and retreating while reloading
can kill a demon at close range with one blast. The chaingun is also substantially effective.
the demon is unable to attack the player when being damaged with the chainsaw, and the chainsaw does not use up any ammunition.

lines.line: Tips: They run fast and in a zig-zag, closing distance quickly and helping to corner you. Lure them into a tight corridor so they cannot swarm you from all directions, and use the chainsaw there. They are generally the easiest monsters to trick into attacking other enemies.

quoted: Due to its speed, the demon closes distances very quickly, often running toward the player in a zig-zag pattern, making it harder to hit, and helping corner the player.

This strategy is especially effective if the player is able to lure the demon(s) into a tight corridor, as they will be able to cut them down without having to worry about being swarmed from all directions.
are generally the easiest monster to trick into attacking other enemies.

lines.line: Summary: A melee weapon that saws anything in reach, roughly a quadruple-speed fist, and it uses no ammo. The Doom 64 version has two blades and the letters U.A.C. engraved on top, and does roughly double the damage of the PC one.

quoted: The chainsaw mutilates enemies close enough to contact.
it is roughly a quadruple-speed fist.
The saw has two blades instead of one and the letters "U.A.C." are engraved on top of the weapon. The damage inflicted by this version of the weapon is roughly doubled
the chainsaw does not use up any ammunition.

lines.line: Uses: Best against demons and spectres, which you can usually kill without taking damage, and fairly effective against cacodemons and imps. Its rapid fire works well on enemies that flinch easily, because it keeps them from hitting back. It is ineffective against Hell knights and other demons with powerful attacks and low pain chance.

quoted: It is most effective against demons and spectres, since the player can usually kill them without taking damage.
It can also be used fairly effectively against cacodemons, pain elementals, lost souls, and imps.
works well on enemies with high pain chance, minimizing damage to the player in melee situations.
It is ineffective against Hell knights and other demons with powerful attacks and low pain chance.

lines.line: Tips: Its reach is only 65 map units, barely more than a fist's 64, so you have to be right on top of the target. Against a pack of demons, back into a corner and saw them down one by one. In open areas with several enemies it is a liability, because it kills more slowly than a berserk fist.

quoted: The chainsaw has a range of 65 map units, slightly larger than the fist's 64 units.
Expert players confronted by a pack of demons and spectres back into a corner and chainsaw them down one by one
The chainsaw's disadvantage is its slow killing speed compared to the berserk fist, which becomes a liability when facing multiple enemies in open areas.

lines.line: Summary: The ultimate weapon: it fires a big ball of green plasma that can destroy nearly any monster in one shot and spreads damage over a wide area. In Doom 64 it has a darker colour scheme and first turns up in MAP10: The Bleeding.

quoted: The BFG9000 is the ultimate weapon to be found in Doom.
it is capable of destroying nearly any player or monster with a single shot, and can disperse damage over a wide area to multiple targets simultaneously.
fires large spheres of green plasma.
in Doom 64, where it is given a new look with a darker color scheme, it is first introduced in MAP10: The Bleeding.

lines.line: Uses: Good for clearing a room. The plasma ball explodes where it hits, and a moment later invisible rays fan out in a cone from you and hurt what they hit. Even cyberdemons, which are immune to blast damage, are hurt by those rays.

quoted: Great for clearing the room of those unwelcome guests.
If this plasma ball hits a solid object, it explodes and randomly deals between 100 and 800 hit points of damage to the target
40 invisible tracer rays are emitted from the player in a cone-shaped volume
Even cyberdemons and spiderdemons, which are immune to blast damage, are affected by these rays.
The damage calculations are mostly the same as in Doom and Doom II

lines.line: Tips: It does not fire the instant you pull the trigger: in Doom 64 there is a wait of exactly one second before the ball leaves, and the rays follow about half a second after it hits. The rays go in the direction the ball was fired even if you turn, so keep facing your target. A shot takes 40 cells, and a BFG you pick up holds 40.

quoted: the slower tic rate causes the weapon to wait exactly 1 second before firing the projectile.
The tracer spray attack upon detonation takes 14 tics to be called instead of 16, which translates to roughly 0.466 seconds.
If the player has turned around, the direction of the rays does not change
When picked up, the BFG contains 40 energy cell units
It expends 40 energy cell units per shot.

lines.line: Summary: A gray-brown orb that sets both your health and your armour to 200 percent; the armour is the same as blue armour. In Doom 64 it shows a helmet like the player's instead of a demonic face.

quoted: Picking it up maxes out both the player's health and armor to 200%. The armor given by a megasphere is equivalent to blue armor.
though in Doom 64 they display a helmet similar to the player's

lines.line: Uses: One pickup tops up both health and armour at once. It counts in the items percentage shown at the end of each level.

quoted: Picking it up maxes out both the player's health and armor to 200%.
Megaspheres are included in the items percentage displayed at the end of each level.

lines.line: Tips: The first one in Doom 64 is in MAP06: Alpha Quadrant, and the game holds nine or ten of them, depending on the skill level.

quoted: || Doom 64 || MAP06: Alpha Quadrant || MAP06: Alpha Quadrant || MAP06: Alpha Quadrant

lines.line: Summary: The double-barrelled sawed-off shotgun: two shells per shot and 20 pellets per blast, about three times as damaging as the normal shotgun per shot. In Doom 64 it reloads much faster, in 1.53 seconds against 1.77 in Doom II, and it knocks you back a little when fired. It is one of the most essential weapons in Doom 64.

quoted: is a sawed-off, break-open, double-barrel shotgun
uses two shells per shot. However, whereas the shotgun fires seven pellets in each shot, a super shotgun blast has 20 pellets.
The super shotgun is about three times as damaging as the standard shotgun per shot
In Doom 64 the super shotgun reloads faster, completing in 1.53s versus 1.77s in Doom II.
In addition, the gun knocks the player back a bit when fired.
This makes it one of the most essential weapons in the game.

lines.line: Uses: One well-aimed blast almost always kills two imps, one demon or one spectre. It lets you hold your own against tough monsters such as Hell knights, arachnotrons and mancubi, and it is often a better choice than the rocket launcher there, because shells are more plentiful than rockets and a short-range rocket blast can hurt you.

quoted: One well-aimed blast from a super shotgun almost always kills two imps, one demon, or one spectre
can enable the player to hold their own against crowds of humanoids or tough monsters (Hell knights, arachnotrons, mancubi).

It is often sensible to prefer the super shotgun over the rocket launcher in such situations; the super shotgun is similarly powerful, shells are more plentiful than rockets, and a short-range rocket blast can harm the player.

lines.line: Tips: The pellets spread wide, even up and down, so it is wasteful at long range: switch to the shotgun to snipe, or to deal with a lone enemy in a maze. It uses the same shells as the shotgun.

quoted: The wide spread of the pellets makes the super shotgun ineffective and wasteful at longer ranges.
unlike other hitscan attacks which only spread horizontally, the SSG's pellets also spread vertically.
it is advisable to switch back to the shotgun
The super shotgun is also a bad choice for dealing with lone humanoids scattered in mazes.
The super shotgun takes the same ammunition as the shotgun

lines.line: Summary: A rapid-fire gun that shoots bursts of blue plasma and shares your energy cells with the BFG9000. In Doom 64 it has a blue electric tube on top that buzzes constantly.

quoted: fires blue and white bursts of plasma. It shares the player's stock of energy cells with the BFG9000 as a source of ammo.
It has a blue electric tube on top, which makes a constant buzzing sound.

lines.line: Uses: It is devastating against nearly any single enemy and can be considered the game's jack-of-all-trades. A continuous barrage stops an arachnotron or a mancubus in its tracks and can slow a baron of Hell to about half its normal speed and attack rate.

quoted: the plasma gun is devastating against nearly any single opponent.
A continuous barrage will stop an arachnotron, mancubus or revenant dead in its tracks, and even reduce a baron of Hell to about half its normal movement speed and attack frequency.
it is a very powerful weapon that can be considered the game's jack-of-all trades.

lines.line: Tips: In Doom 64 it fires a little slower than on PC, one shot every 0.133 seconds, but there is no pause after you let go of the trigger and the shots travel faster. At long range enemies tend to move too much for a burst to hit, so fire in controlled bursts rather than holding the trigger.

quoted: it fires at a slower rate of one projectile every 4 tics.
this translates to one projectile every 0.133 seconds.
If the trigger is released, there is no cooldown pause and the weapon is immediately ready to fire again.
they have a faster travel speed of 40 units per tic.
enemies tend to move too much for the bursts to be accurate
A good tactic to counter this weakness is to fire the plasma gun in controlled bursts, as opposed to fully automatic fire.

lines.line: Summary: A dark gray medikit that raises your health to 100 percent if it was lower and makes your punches far stronger. It also fills the screen with a red haze, which lasts only three seconds in Doom 64.

quoted: is an item that looks like a dark gray medikit.
Picking one up greatly increases the damage the player inflicts with their fists, and boosts the player's health to the full normal amount (100 percent, unless it was already 100 or more).
The red haze lasts approximately 20 seconds, except in Doom 64 where it is three seconds.

lines.line: Uses: It makes your punch ten times stronger, usually until the level ends or you die: enough to smash humanoids to a pulp, or sometimes kill a demon in one blow. Your current weapon switches to the fist when you pick it up, so you can end up suddenly unarmed.

quoted: The berserk pack increases the strength of the player's punch attack tenfold, typically until the current level ends or the player dies.
The damage increase is powerful enough to often smash humanoids to a pulp, or even sometimes kill a demon with a single blow.
When a berserk pack is collected, the player's current weapon will switch to the fist.
Players grabbing the powerup quickly may find themselves suddenly unarmed

lines.line: Tips: The extra strength does not run out when the red haze fades, so do not stop punching because the screen has cleared. Use it hit-and-run: run up, punch, then retreat or dodge. A punch does not latch on like the chainsaw, so aim carefully.

quoted: since it kills quicker and does not "latch" on enemies.
This effect might confuse new players, who often believe that the berserk pack's effects last only as long as the red haze is on screen
Due to its power, the berserk punch is best used for hit-and-run situations, running up to the foe to throw a punch and then quickly retreating or dodging.
Berserk however has the disadvantage of not doing continuous damage, which leaves the player more open to counterattacks, and requires relatively careful aim.
